name: China's Century of Upheaval: Qing to People's Republic
description: From opium wars and rebellions to the fall of the last dynasty, civil war, famine and reform: how China was remade between 1839 and 1989.

checkpoints.name: An empire under strain
checkpoints.note: The Qing dynasty ruled China for centuries. Britain won the First Opium War, and under the 1842 Treaty of Nanking took Hong Kong island, which became British Hong Kong. The defeat showed how weak the empire had become.

checkpoints.name: Rebellion and reform
checkpoints.note: The Taiping Rebellion became one of history's deadliest wars. Empress Dowager Cixi held power at court, Japan beat China in the First Sino-Japanese War of 1894 to 1895, the Boxer Rebellion was put down by foreign armies, and Sun Yat-sen plotted for a republic.

checkpoints.name: The fall of the last dynasty
checkpoints.note: The Xinhai Revolution of 1911 led the child emperor Puyi to abdicate, and the Republic of China began in 1912. The Kuomintang was founded, and the Chinese Communist Party followed in 1921.

checkpoints.name: War at home and abroad
checkpoints.note: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists and the Communists fought the Chinese Civil War. Japan set up Manchukuo in 1932 and in 1937 began a full invasion, the Second Sino-Japanese War, marked by atrocities such as the Nanjing Massacre. Mao Zedong rose to lead the Communist forces.

checkpoints.name: The People's Republic
checkpoints.note: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949, with Zhou Enlai as its first premier, while the Nationalists withdrew to Taiwan. The Great Leap Forward of 1958 led to the Great Chinese Famine, which killed millions, and the Cultural Revolution, with its Little Red Book of Quotations from Chairman Mao, followed.

checkpoints.name: Reform and protest
checkpoints.note: Deng Xiaoping opened China to markets and foreign trade. In 1989 students and others gathered in Tiananmen Square, and the protests were ended by the army.
